title: Establish semantic structure and focus order
description: Use native landmarks, headings, labels, roles, values, instructions, skip navigation, and logical visible focus order to communicate application structure and control purpose across primary screens.
acceptanceCriteria: Each primary screen has one clear main landmark, ordered headings, and named navigation regions
Interactive controls expose accurate accessible names, roles, states, values, and instructions
Tab order follows visible reading and workflow order without positive tabindex
Focus is visibly distinguishable and skip navigation reaches primary content
Preview and grid meaning has a textual semantic alternative

steps.details: Review landmark, heading, form, table/grid, dialog, and accessible-name structure on representative primary states.
Replace generic clickable elements with native controls and add ARIA only where no native pattern expresses the required state.
Align DOM and visible order, remove positive tabindex, add skip navigation, and ensure a persistent visible focus indicator.
Use role/name queries and keyboard traversal checks on representative editor, preparation, calibration, and recovery screens.

technicalNotes: Maximum execution scope is ten minutes; address a bounded representative screen set and focused tests.
Do not add redundant or conflicting ARIA where native HTML already provides semantics.
